title: Six open models match a Blackwell start. That is not a map of the chips.
friendlyTitle: Six open models look like they started on Blackwell chips. That does not show where the chips are.
summary: On 12 November, Will DePue published a forensic read of public model weights. Six models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group match the starting pattern of NVIDIA Blackwell chips. DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 match a B200 or B300. DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro, and Ling-3.1-flash match a GB200 or GB300. Earlier models from the same labs match the older Hopper pattern. The newest readable models from Alibaba, Zhipu, Tencent, Xiaomi, and StepFun still read as Hopper.
friendlySummary: On 12 November, Will DePue published a study of public model files. Six models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group match the starting pattern of NVIDIA's newer Blackwell chips. Older models from the same labs match the previous chip generation. The newest readable models from Alibaba, Zhipu, Tencent, Xiaomi, and StepFun still match the older chips.
whyItMatters: The method agreed with the hardware a lab had already named, in all 24 cases he checked. It does not show where the chips were, how they were reached, or whether an export rule was broken. A specially configured AMD machine is the only other match he found, and he says he has ruled that out for DeepSeek-V4-Flash. A fingerprint in the weights is evidence of a starting chip, not a charge.
